raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Currently ring attention cannot run with the AITER backend on ROCm. This PR makes AITER backend ring-compatible and returns LSE on request. This PR also changes the default ROCm backend selection when using ring. AITER is the default backend when ring attention is selected. Note: this PR previously also reworked `USPAttention` to handle replicated prefix/suffix tokens under ulysses+ring. #33327 has since solved that properly via `USPAttention._replicated_kv_attention`, which LSE-merges the replicated KV with the ring-sharded KV, so that work has been dropped and this PR has been rebased and trimmed to the AITER/ROCm half. ## Modifications - `AITerImpl.forward` takes `return_softmax_lse` and returns the BF16 kernel's LSE, and `AITerBackend.supports_ring_rotation()` declares the capability. The FP8 FMHA ASM path has no LSE output, so it yields to the BF16 kernel when an LSE is requested. - Adds `aiter` to `RING_CAPABLE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, the name-level admission list that gates before backend classes are importable on every platform. - Returns AITER as backend by default when using ring and no attention backend is specified - Drops the AMD/ROCm ring skip in the server test fixture, and extends `test_ring_admission.py` with a ROCm-gated case pinning the name list to the backend capability. ## Accuracy Tests Run command: ``` sglang generate --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev \ --num-gpus 4 --ulysses-degree 2 --ring-degree 2 \ --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-inference-steps 28 --seed 42 \ --prompt "A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets" ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. nodes.body: @mickqian Is this good to go? :) I don't think the CI ran? No run-ci tag, at least.

Thanks for this, and sorry it sat so long! Since then, #33327 added ring support for replicated prefix/suffix tokens (`USPAttention._replicated_kv_attention` merges the replicated KV with the ring-sharded KV via LSE), so `_shard_replicated_and_forward` is no longer needed. The AITER part is still missing on main: `aiter.py` doesn't return the softmax LSE and `aiter` isn't in `RING_CAPABLE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, so ring attention can't run with AITER on ROCm. Could you rebase and trim this PR to (1) AITER `return_softmax_lse` plus registering it as ring-capable, and (2) the ROCm fallback preferring AITER over SDPA? Happy to re-review once it's updated.

## Code Review

This pull request enables Ring Attention support for the AITER backend and improves backend selection logic on ROCm platforms. Key changes include updating the AITER attention forward pass to optionally return softmax LSE, implementing a sharding mechanism for replicated tokens in USPAttention when ring parallelism is active, and prioritizing the AITER backend on ROCm. Review feedback suggests updating return type hints for consistency and using established helper functions for sequence parallel rank and size to avoid potential attribute errors.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `sp_group.rank_in_group` might lead to an `AttributeError` as `ParallelGroup` objects in this codebase typically use `.rank` or the provided helper functions. It is safer and more consistent to use `get_sp_world_size()` and `get_sp_parallel_rank()` which are already imported and used elsewhere in this file.

```suggestion
        total_sp_size = get_sp_world_size()
        sp_rank = get_sp_parallel_rank()
```

nodes.body: Thanks for fixing this path. I left one correctness issue inline that I think should be addressed before merge. Also, this PR currently conflicts with current main in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`; after rebasing, please make sure AITER's newer FP8/MLA path also supports `return_softmax_lse=True` for ring attention, or is explicitly bypassed there. It would also be good to add/enable coverage for ROCm + AITER + `ring_degree > 1`, since the existing AMD server tests skip ring attention.

I think this padding is not numerically safe. The padded K/V rows are still visible to the attention softmax, so they consume probability mass even though V is zero. For `num_rep` values that are not divisible by `total_sp_size`, this will silently change outputs rather than just making the replicated tokens shardable. Please either reject this case for now (`num_rep % total_sp_size == 0`) until masking is wired through, or pass a valid-token mask/length into the ring path so padded K/V tokens are excluded from attention.

nodes.body: I removed the padding and added an assertion there instead. FLUX etc. have a fixed length encoder, so they don't run into issues with this, but some other models can. The proper fix there would be to wire in the varlen functions, but that is beyond this PR. So now Ulysses, Ring and Ulysses+Ring all produce good output. The ring-only implementation not touched by this PR is slightly incorrect, as the text tokens are replicated too many times. That can be fixed as well when the masking is supported. Ulysses: Ring+Ulysses: Ring: AMD tests are also now enabled :)

inline_comments.body: I think this padding is not numerically safe. The padded K/V rows are still visible to the attention softmax, so they consume probability mass even though V is zero. For `num_rep` values that are not divisible by `total_sp_size`, this will silently change outputs rather than just making the replicated tokens shardable. Please either reject this case for now (`num_rep % total_sp_size == 0`) until masking is wired through, or pass a valid-token mask/length into the ring path so padded K/V tokens are excluded from attention.

Thanks for this, and sorry it sat so long! Since then, #33327 added ring support for replicated prefix/suffix tokens (`USPAttention._replicated_kv_attention` merges the replicated KV with the ring-sharded KV via LSE), so `_shard_replicated_and_forward` is no longer needed. The AITER part is still missing on main: `aiter.py` doesn't return the softmax LSE and `aiter` isn't in `RING_CAPABLE_ATTENTION_BACKENDS`, so ring attention can't run with AITER on ROCm. Could you rebase and trim this PR to (1) AITER `return_softmax_lse` plus registering it as ring-capable, and (2) the ROCm fallback preferring AITER over SDPA? Happy to re-review once it's updated.

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request enables Ring Attention support for the AITER backend and improves backend selection logic on ROCm platforms. Key changes include updating the AITER attention forward pass to optionally return softmax LSE, implementing a sharding mechanism for replicated tokens in USPAttention when ring parallelism is active, and prioritizing the AITER backend on ROCm. Review feedback suggests updating return type hints for consistency and using established helper functions for sequence parallel rank and size to avoid potential attribute errors.

Thanks for fixing this path. I left one correctness issue inline that I think should be addressed before merge. Also, this PR currently conflicts with current main in `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`; after rebasing, please make sure AITER's newer FP8/MLA path also supports `return_softmax_lse=True` for ring attention, or is explicitly bypassed there. It would also be good to add/enable coverage for ROCm + AITER + `ring_degree > 1`, since the existing AMD server tests skip ring attention.
